data: This course will help students develop conceptual frameworks for exploring the arts as cultural practice and aesthetic experience. Concepts and issues in the study of expressive cultures will be introduced by drawing on periods, movements, genres and traditions from different world art cultures. The course will interweave experiential and analytical learning with socio-historic and critical interpretations, drawing on a variety of examples. Thematic units in the course include a consideration of art as experience; sensing, perceiving and feeling as cultural praxis; meaning making; social organization of cultural practices; power, identity and the politics of representation. Examples could be drawn from ancient, medieval, pre-modern, postcolonial and contemporary periods. Throughout the course, students will be encouraged to apply conceptual learnings to a cultural practice of their choice, giving them an opportunity to deepen their learnings from the course through immersive experience.
